🏘️ HARVEST VILLAGE (formerly Harvest Roaring Fork): DOES ELIMINATING ADUs ACTUALLY LOWER THE PROJECT’S DENSITY AND IMPACTS?
One of the changes highlighted in the “new” Harvest Village application is a prohibition on accessory dwelling units (ADUs).

The developer SAYS this “reduces overall project density by at least 450 residential units.”

That SOUNDS significant. But when you LOOK AT THE UNDERLYING NUMBERS, there is an important distinction. 🔎

🏠 THE NEW PUD STILL PROPOSES UP TO 1,500 RESIDENTIAL UNITS. THAT NUMBER HAS NOT CHANGED.

So what does the “450-unit reduction” ACTUALLY mean?

It appears to refer to “potential, maybe-later-someday, additional housing units IF a homeowner CHOOSES to build an ADU in the future” — NOT 450 HOMES ACTUALLY BEING REMOVED from the proposed 1,500-unit Development Application.

In other words, those 450 units weren't 450 homes being removed from the proposed development. They were hypothetical additional ADUs that might have been built in the future if individual homeowners chose to construct them.

⚠️ AND HERE IS WHERE IT GETS REALLY IMPORTANT:

🚗 WHAT DOES THE TRAFFIC STUDY ACTUALLY MODEL?

🚗 BOTH THE PREVIOUS AND NEW APPLICATIONS’ TRAFFIC ANALYSIS MODEL 1,500 RESIDENTIAL UNITS (without ADUs):

• 450 single-family detached

• 200 single-family attached

• 625 multifamily

• 225 affordable housing

= 1,500 TOTAL RESIDENTIAL UNITS

There was no separate ADU category in that traffic calculation previously, or currently.

The resulting analysis STILL PROJECTS APPROXIMATELY 11,936 WEEKDAY VEHICLE TRIPS AT BUILD OUT. 🚗🚗🚗

So if the ADUs weren't separately included in the traffic model to begin with, eliminating the potential ADUs does not appear to reduce the traffic impacts that were actually analyzed.

📌 THAT’S AN IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:

REDUCING “THEORETICAL” DEVELOPMENT CAPACITY DOES NOT REDUCE THE TRAFFIC IMPACTS FOR THE 1,500-UNIT DEVELOPMENT APPLICATION.

💧 AND WE SHOULD ASK THE SAME QUESTION ABOUT WATER.

The previous application calculated approximately 661 acre-feet of annual water demand.

💦 That translates into approximately 215.4 MILLION GALLONS OF WATER PER YEAR.

The “NEW” Harvest Village Development Application continues to rely, at least in part, on water documentation prepared for the previous Harvest Roaring Fork application, including a NOVEMBER 2024 Waterlaw letter.

What is not clear from this Exhibit is whether the “newly revised” development has a NEW, TRANSPARENT 2026 water-demand calculation showing how much water the revised project is actually expected to require.

That is a question we should be asking.

So rather than SIMPLY ACCEPTING the “statement” from the developer that the project is “reduced by 450 units,” 

THE REASONABLE PUBLIC QUESTION IS:

❓ WHAT NUMBERS ACTUALLY CHANGED?

🏠 DID THE NUMBER OF HOMES IN THE DEVELOPMENT APPLICATION CHANGE?

No — it remains up to 1,500. As it was before.

🚗 DID THE TRAFFIC MODEL REMOVE TRIPS ASSOCIATED WITH ADUs?

No — the traffic model doesn't appear to have separately included them in the first place.

💧 DID THE WATER-DEMAND CALCULATION DECREASE BECAUSE ADUs WERE ELIMINATED?

No — the current application is still using the water calculations from the previous application.

In other words, the water-demand numbers haven't changed to reflect the elimination of the potential ADUs.

This isn't about being for or against Harvest Village.

It's about making sure that when we are TOLD a proposed development application has been MEANINGFULLY REDUCED, the underlying impact numbers regarding water and traffic SHOULD DEMONSTRATE THAT REDUCTION.

📊 THAT’S WHAT THE PUBLIC DESERVES TO SEE.

⚠️ IF YOU SUBMITTED WRITTEN COMMENTS FOR HARVEST ROARING FORK, THOSE ARE NO LONGER VALID FOR THE “NEW” HARVEST APPLICATION!

Please DM me for a template letter, contact information as well as a link to the Cattle Creek Confluence Coalition's website where you can find much more information on this new application.
